# Exact affine-root counterexample with step budgets, and its simplex realization

The numerical closure considered here assumes: d>=2; the complete integer
interval I; positive affine captured roots a_j; a source i with a_i=k>=r_d;
critical balance sum(j-i)a_j^(d-1)=0; positive concave whole roots v>=a with
v_i=1; both step comparisons

    B:=sum a_j^d <= k^d+sum_{j<i}v_j^d,
    B <= k^d+sum_{j>i}v_j^d;

and the additional comparison B>=Gamma_d max_j v_j^d. These assumptions do
NOT imply sum v_j^d<=2B/Gamma_d. The failure below even has k=r_d exactly.

The second part realizes the scalar data by actual homothetic simplex
fibers. The chosen cap is a global minimizer among ALL integer tilts with
its fixed continuous normal. Nevertheless a different mixed-integer point
has strictly greater halfspace depth. Thus other candidate centers are a
material missing invariant. This is not an (OC) counterexample.

## 1. Ten-site scalar counterexample with exact own fraction

Set d=6, I={0,...,9}, i=8, r=6/7, Gamma=r^6. Let c be the unique positive
root of

    P(c)=35c^5+375c^4+2550c^3+8670c^2+9195c-11805.

The derivative is positive on [0,infinity), and

    P(2/3)=-239945/243<0,
    P(3/4)=1198965/1024>0.

Thus 2/3<c<3/4. Define

    a_j = r (j+c)/(8+c),
    v_j = (67+j)/75 = 1+(j-8)/75.

Both sequences are strictly positive and affine. They satisfy v_8=1 and
k=a_8=r. The inequality v>=a follows by checking the two endpoints:

    a_0 < r*(3/4)/(8+3/4)=18/245 < 67/75=v_0,
    a_9 < r*(9+2/3)/(8+2/3)=87/91 < 76/75=v_9.

The finite polynomial identity

    sum_{j=0}^9(j-8)(j+c)^5=-P(c)

gives sum(j-8)a_j^5=0 exactly.

### An exact captured-mass upper bound

For t>0 put B(t)=r^6 sum_{j=0}^9(j+t)^6/(8+t)^6. Differentiation gives

    B'(t)=6r^6 P(t)/(8+t)^7.

Since P is increasing and vanishes at c, B(t) is minimized at c. Therefore

    B=B(c) <= B(2/3)
      =837979292565/567869252041 <369/250.

The final strict comparison follows from

    369*567869252041-250*837979292565=48930861879>0.

### Both step comparisons

First, Gamma>79/200, since

    200*6^6-79*7^6=36929>0.

By the binomial theorem,

    Gamma+v_9^6
      >79/200+1+6/75+15/75^2
      =369/250+1/600 >B.

This is the right step comparison. For the left one, v_j>=67/75 and

    2*67^6-75^6=2938248713>0,

so sum_{j<8}v_j^6>8/2=4>B. Adding the source cap only strengthens it.

### The largest-fiber comparison

Since a_9>a_8=r, one has B>2Gamma. Also v_9<11/10 and
(11/10)^6<2. Thus

    Gamma max_j v_j^6=Gamma v_9^6<2Gamma<B.

### Strict failure of the proposed conclusion

The total whole-fiber mass is exactly

    M=sum_{j=0}^9v_j^6=273705308393/35595703125 >23/3,

because 3*273705308393-23*35595703125=2414753304>0. Also

    Gamma>9/23,

because 23*6^6-9*7^6=14247>0. Consequently

    Gamma M>3>738/250>2B.

Equivalently M>2B/Gamma, with all the stated numerical premises satisfied.

## 2. Actual simplex fibers realize every scalar datum

Choose a six-dimensional simplex T of volume one and centroid zero. Choose
a linear functional ell that takes value r=6/7 at one vertex and -1/7 at
all other vertices. Such a functional exists because these seven values
sum to zero; the only affine dependence on the seven affinely independent
vertices compatible with a linear functional through the centroid is
exactly this mean-zero condition. Its range width is one. Homothetic
simplex caps therefore have the exact upper-tail formula

    |vT intersect {ell(x)>=s}|
      =clamp(rv-s,0,v)^6,                                 (1)

where clamp(t,0,v)=min(v,max(0,t)). This includes empty, full, and supporting
cuts; supporting hyperplanes have zero six-dimensional boundary measure.

Let v(t)=(67+t)/75 and form the actual convex body

    C={(t,x):0<=t<=9, x in v(t)T}.

Convexity follows directly from the affine positive scale v and convexity
of T. Compactness and nonempty ambient interior are immediate. Its
mixed-integer set has exactly the ten fibers C_j=v_jT. Put y=(8,0), which
belongs to C_8 and hence to S. Define

    s_* = r/(8+c),       lambda = r/75-s_*,
    H_* = {(t,x):ell(x)>=lambda(t-8)}.

At each integer j, (1) has unclipped root

    r v_j-lambda(j-8)=r+s_*(j-8)=a_j.

The endpoint checks in Section 1 show 0<a_j<v_j for every j, so every cut
is proper and the captured masses are exactly a_j^6. Its total mass is B.
The point y is the ordinary centroid of its fiber, and H_* goes through y.

## 3. There is no better integer tilt with this fixed normal

Every halfspace through y with continuous normal ell has the same form,
with an arbitrary lambda, and its mass can equivalently be parameterized
by s=r/75-lambda:

    Q(s)=sum_{j=0}^9 clamp(r+s(j-8),0,v_j)^6.              (2)

We prove Q(s)>=B for every real s, with equality at s=s_*.

For s<0 and j<=8, the unclipped root is at least r. Since every v_j>=67/75>r,
these nine fibers each contribute at least r^6=Gamma. Thus

    Q(s)>=9Gamma>9*(79/200)>B.

Put s_R=v_9-r>0. For 0<=s<=s_R there is no upper clipping: the left eight
unclipped roots are at most r<v_j, the own root equals r<1, and the right
root r+s is at most v_9. Hence

    Q(s)=sum_{j=0}^9 [r+s(j-8)]_+^6

throughout this interval, a convex function of s. The chosen s_* lies
strictly inside this interval, since all its cuts are proper. Its derivative
is 6sum(j-8)a_j^5=0. Convexity therefore proves Q(s)>=Q(s_*)=B throughout
the entire interval, including every zero-root crossing.

For s>=s_R the right fiber is wholly captured. The source contributes
Gamma, so

    Q(s)>=Gamma+v_9^6>B

by the exact step comparison. This proves global integer-tilt minimality,
not merely stationarity inside the proper-cut cell. It does not assert
minimality over changes of the continuous normal.

## 4. Another actual mixed-integer point is strictly deeper

Take y'=(4,0). Since 0 is in the interior of T and v_j>=v_0, the actual
mixed-integer subset

    S_core={0,...,8} x (v_0 T)

is contained in S. Its center y' belongs to S.

We use the already proved ordinary paired-centroid-tail inequality from
`candidate 732b11a769399016`, Section 1:
for a centroided d-body K and every nonzero linear functional u,

    |K intersect {u.x>=t}|+|K intersect {u.x>=-t}|
        >=2 Gamma_d |K|                                  (3)

for every real t, including empty/full/support-endpoint thresholds. This
is an ordinary continuous theorem; its complete proof and localization
conditions are recorded in that source, independently of (OC).

For any ambient halfspace through y' with nonzero continuous normal, the
source core fiber contributes at least Gamma v_0^6 by ordinary Gruenbaum.
The four pairs of core fibers indexed 4-l and 4+l have opposite thresholds.
Each pair contributes at least 2Gamma v_0^6 by (3). Thus every such
halfspace contains at least 9Gamma v_0^6 core mass.

If the continuous normal is zero, a closed halfspace through the middle
integer 4 contains at least five of the nine core fibers. Its mass is at
least 5v_0^6>=9Gamma v_0^6, since Gamma<1/2. A closed halfspace merely
containing y' can be translated parallel to itself until its boundary goes
through y', which only decreases its intersection. Thus the same bound
holds for EVERY closed ambient halfspace containing y'.

Finally the exact inequalities from Section 1 imply

    9Gamma v_0^6>9*(79/200)*(1/2)=711/400>369/250>B.

Therefore the actual raw halfspace depth at y' is strictly greater than B,
whereas the depth at y is at most B because H_* contains y. Normalizing both
by the same total mass M preserves the strict inequality. Hence y is not a
globally deepest point. The scalar largest-fiber comparison and the two
step comparisons fail to encode this stronger competing-center condition.

### A simpler exact exclusion using only ordinary Gruenbaum

The quantitative exclusion does not need paired tails. All ten fiber
centroids are (j,0), so they lie on an affine line. Their weights are
w_j=v_j^6. The integer j=6 is an exact weighted median: with
L_6=sum_{j<6}w_j and R_6=sum_{j>6}w_j, rational arithmetic gives

    M-2L_6=3911779367/177978515625>0,
    M-2R_6=99585557737/59326171875>0.

Every ambient closed halfspace containing (6,0) intersects this centroid
line in a closed halfline or the entire line. Its included fiber centroids
therefore carry weight at least M/2. In each such fiber ordinary continuous
Gruenbaum gives captured volume at least Gamma times the full fiber volume.
Summing the disjoint fibers proves depth at (6,0) at least Gamma M/2.
Section 1 gives the strict quantitative comparison

    Gamma M/2>3/2>369/250>B.

This is precisely the full-contact case of the archived theorem
`candidate 8c2b392c7a2005ed`: the positive whole-fiber
roots v_j agree everywhere with a global affine majorant, so its contact
mass equals M. The direct weighted-median argument above proves this
particular application without any compactness, stability theorem, or
loss in the exact Gamma/2 constant. It requires only affine alignment of
the fiber centroids and is therefore valid even without homothety once that
alignment has independently been established.

## 5. The earlier seventy-one-site certificate

For completeness, the first strengthened counter found before the smaller
one also has an exact certificate. Set d=6, I={0,...,70}, i=60, and let c be
the unique positive root of

    P_71(c)=5c^5+455c^4+23450c^3+626878c^2+6155485c-24348077.

Its positive derivative and values P_71(2)=-9334555, P_71(3)=431500 give
2<c<3. Set a_j=(j+c)/(70+c), v_j=(540+j)/600. Then

    sum(j-60)(j+c)^5=-355P_71(c),
    k=(60+c)/(70+c)>6/7,
    B<B(3)=1654903372484/151334226289<219/20.

The last inequality has positive cross-product difference 44128107611.
The affine endpoint comparisons give v>=a. Moreover k>31/36 and
(31/36)^6>2/5, while the right ten fibers have total mass greater than
10+6*(1+...+10)/600=211/20. Thus the right step budget exceeds 219/20>B.
The left budget is larger than 60*(9/10)^6>B. Also
Gamma maxv^6=(61/70)^6<1<B, since a_70=1 and the other cap masses are
positive. Finally

    M=523011847458152767/9331200000000000>56,
    Gamma>11/28,

so Gamma M>22>2B. These are exact alternatives, but the ten-site version
above is stronger because k=r exactly and its actual competing center has
an especially simple certificate.
